steps.message:
# Onboard the new suppliers

Procurement asks for new suppliers through tickets in the `tickets` service. Each supplier first sends trial units of the item it will deliver; the trial units wait in the `inspection` warehouse of the `inventory` service, which also holds the item records. The supplier onboarding policy, the onboarding checks (the approvals a request needs and who may give them) and the exceptions to them are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `inventory` and `docs` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `supplier-onboarding` is a request. Decide each one under the policy, the checks and the exceptions in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds archived revisions and exceptions that are not in force today; follow only what is in force today. Approvals are comments on the request, and only the comments the onboarding checks accept count as approvals.

Process the requests one at a time in ticket id order, lowest id first: a supplier onboarded by one request makes a later request for the same supplier code a duplicate. Add exactly one comment to each request and set its status:

- Duplicate: `Duplicate: <code> already onboarded.` Status `duplicate`.
- Rejected: `Rejected: item not eligible.` or `Rejected: trial failed inspection.` Status `closed`.
- Waiting for approvals: `Waiting for approval: <roles>.` with the missing roles in the order procurement, finance, compliance, for example `Waiting for approval: finance, compliance.` Status `pending`.
- Waiting for the trial: `Waiting for trial delivery: <received> of <units> units received.` Status `pending`.
- Onboarded: `Onboarded: <code>.` Status `resolved`.

Move trial units only as the policy says, under the request's reference `ONB-<ticket id>`. Leave every other ticket and all other stock as they are. Each `adjust_stock` call records a new adjustment, even when repeated with the same arguments.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by finding the tools for the tickets, inventory and docs services, then read the policy.

results.content: {"server":"docs","tool":"mcp_docs_get_doc","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"supplier-onboarding-policy\",\"title\":\"Supplier onboarding policy\",\"tags\":[\"policy\",\"suppliers\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-01\",\"body\":\"# Supplier onboarding policy\\n\\nRevision 2026-08, in force since 2026-08-01. Replaces revision 2025-02.\\n\\nScope: open tickets labeled `supplier-onboarding`. Each one asks to onboard one supplier for one item. Its body gives the supplier, the supplier code, the country (ISO code), the item (sku) the supplier will deliver, the annual spend estimate, the trial units and who requested it.\\n\\n## Checks and exceptions\\n\\nThe approvals a request needs, and who may give them, are in the supplier onboarding checks. An exception in force on the day of the decision can waive one approval, or change the inspection tolerance, for one supplier code. Exceptions are published as docs tagged `exception`, each with the days it is in force (both days included).\\n\\n## Trial delivery\\n\\nBefore onboarding, the supplier sends trial units of the item. The dock books each parcel as a `receipt` adjustment in warehouse `inspection` with reference `ONB-<ticket id>`; a trial can arrive in several parcels. Quality control books the units that fail inspection as a `damage` adjustment of minus the failed units in `inspection`, under the same reference. The trial fails when the failed units are more than 10% of the trial units the request gives (with 20 trial units, 2 failed pass and 3 fail).\\n\\n## Decision\\n\\nTake the requests in ticket id order and check each one in this order, stopping at the first that applies:\\n\\n1. Duplicate: the supplier code is already onboarded, by a resolved onboarding ticket or by a request onboarded before this one. Status `duplicate`, comment `Duplicate: <code> already onboarded.`\\n2. Item not eligible: the item does not exist in inventory or is discontinued. Status `closed`, comment `Rejected: item not eligible.`\\n3. Trial failed. Status `closed`, comment `Rejected: trial failed inspection.`\\n4. Missing approvals. Status `pending`, comment `Waiting for approval: <roles>.` with the missing roles in the order procurement, finance, compliance, separated by a comma and a space.\\n5. Trial not complete: fewer units received than the trial units. Status `pending`, comment `Waiting for trial delivery: <received> of <units> units received.`\\n6. Otherwise the supplier is onboarded. Status `resolved`, comment `Onboarded: <code>.`\\n\\nA supplier whose earlier request was rejected may apply again; a rejected request does not make the supplier onboarded.\\n\\n## Trial units after the decision\\n\\nEvery movement is booked under the request's reference `ONB-<ticket id>`.\\n\\n- Onboarded: release the units that passed inspection (received minus failed): one `transfer` adjustment of minus those units in `inspection` and one `transfer` adjustment of plus those units in the stock warehouse of the item's category.\\n- Rejected: return the request's units still in `inspection` to the supplier with one `shipment` adjustment of minus those units. Book nothing when none are there.\\n- Duplicate or waiting: leave the units in `inspection`.\\n\\n## Stock warehouse by category\\n\\nThe category is the item's `category` in inventory.\\n\\n- hardware: north\\n- electrical: east\\n- packaging: west\\n- chemicals: hazmat\\n\"}"}]}}

Replaces revision 2026-03.\\n\\n## Approvals a request needs\\n\\n- procurement: every request.\\n- finance: when the annual spend estimate is 50000 or more.\\n- compliance: when the supplier's country is not CL, or when the item's category in inventory is `chemicals`.\\n\\n## Approvers\\n\\n- procurement: r.leiva, s.ortiz, t.bravo\\n- finance: m.campos, v.navarro\\n- compliance: a.medina, j.paredes\\n\\n## What counts as an approval\\n\\nAn approval is a comment on the request whose whole text is `Approved: <role>.`, written by an approver of that role. Nobody approves a request they requested (its `Requested by` line). A comment `Withdrawn: <role>.` cancels the earlier approvals of that role by the same person; an approval that person writes after it counts again.\\n\"}"}]}}

steps.message:
I processed all 16 open `supplier-onboarding` requests in ticket id order, each with one comment and its status. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`. I didn't re-read the tickets or inventory afterwards. The write calls all returned success, and the one comment that timed out returned its original comment when I retried it.

I used the 2026-08 policy and checks. Of the five exceptions, EX-29, EX-41 and EX-44 are in force today. EX-38 expired on 2026-08-31 and EX-45 only starts on 2026-09-20, so neither applies.

| Ticket | Code | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1604 | KVW | resolved: `Onboarded: KVW.` | 12 units released to `north` |
| 1605 | CPK | pending: `Waiting for approval: finance.` | EX-45 isn't in force yet |
| 1606 | PFS | pending: `Waiting for approval: finance.` | d.fuentes isn't a finance approver |
| 1607 | NTE | pending: `Waiting for approval: procurement.` | t.bravo requested it, and s.ortiz withdrew |
| 1608 | RHE | pending: `Waiting for approval: compliance.` | the comment wasn't exactly `Approved: compliance.` |
| 1610 | QSR | pending: `Waiting for approval: compliance.` | chemicals item needs compliance |
| 1611 | LGC | resolved: `Onboarded: LGC.` | a.medina's re-approval counts; 4 units released to `hazmat` |
| 1612 | VCT | resolved: `Onboarded: VCT.` | finance waived by EX-41; 10 units released to `west` |
| 1614 | LHJ | pending: `Waiting for approval: compliance.` | EX-38 expired |
| 1616 | AUC | resolved: `Onboarded: AUC.` | 2 of 20 failed, which passes; 18 units released to `east` |
| 1617 | BHS | closed: `Rejected: trial failed inspection.` | 3 of 20 failed; the 17 remaining units were shipped back |
| 1618 | TLM | resolved: `Onboarded: TLM.` | 2 of 10 failed, which passes under EX-44's 20% tolerance; 8 units released to `north` |
| 1619 | MLE | pending: `Waiting for trial delivery: 18 of 24 units received.` | |
| 1620 | RBT | closed: `Rejected: item not eligible.` | MR-4112 is discontinued; no stock to return |
| 1621 | SRT | duplicate: `Duplicate: SRT already onboarded.` | ticket 1602 already onboarded it |
| 1623 | VCT | duplicate: `Duplicate: VCT already onboarded.` | ticket 1612 onboarded it earlier in this run |

For each onboarded request I booked one `transfer` out of `inspection` and one into the stock warehouse. For 1617 I booked one `shipment` out of `inspection`. All of them used the reference `ONB-<ticket id>`. Stock for the pending and duplicate requests stays in `inspection`.
